fixes.explanation: Fire from the sky isn't here, friend. The LORD says they “…will die from deadly diseases.” and be “…finished off by sword and famine…” (Jeremiah 16:4) This is a heavy verse. The text names diseases, sword and famine, and that's what we stick with.

You read it right, baker. The LORD says, “They will not be mourned or buried, but will lie like dung on the ground.” (Jeremiah 16:4) Nobody will mourn them and nobody will bury them. Good that you read it carefully.

Careful, friend, because the verse says the opposite. The LORD says, “No food will be offered to comfort those who mourn the dead; not even a cup of consolation will be given for the loss of a father or mother.” (Jeremiah 16:7) So the answer is False. No food will be offered for comfort here.

That's it, baker. The LORD says they will say He brought the Israelites up “…out of the land of the north and all the other lands to which He had banished them.” (Jeremiah 16:15) They will no longer say the saying about Egypt (Jeremiah 16:14). They will say this new one instead. Something big is coming for them.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and hill, even from the clefts of the rocks.” (Jeremiah 16:16) First fishermen, then hunters.

Right, baker. The LORD says, “For My eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from My face, and their guilt is not concealed from My eyes.” (Jeremiah 16:17) Not some of their ways, but all of them.
Yes, baker. The words to the LORD say, “…the nations will come to You from the ends of the earth…” (Jeremiah 16:19) After all that heavy news, the view widens way out. Now it's nations coming to Him.

Not quite, friend, because this one is in the verse. The words to the LORD say, “…the nations will come to You from the ends of the earth…” (Jeremiah 16:19) So the answer is True. The message opens up from one people to nations coming to Him.
That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “…I will make them know My power and My might; then they will know that My name is the LORD.” (Jeremiah 16:21) The message ends on who He is.

Not this time, friend. Earlier in the passage, the nations are the ones who will say, “Our fathers inherited nothing but lies…” (Jeremiah 16:19) The LORD says, “then they will know that My name is the LORD.” (Jeremiah 16:21) That's what they come to know.
